title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

reading.body:
Instinct is an AI personal assistant that uses personal information shared with it for model training unless users actively opt out. The system retains copies of data from previously linked accounts indefinitely even after disconnection, meaning user information persists in the system beyond active access. The assistant can make purchases on users' behalf using stored payment methods, and the company disclaims responsibility for purchase disputes.

This shows a deployment where data practices and autonomous capabilities were not clearly communicated to users at signup. It would have taken transparency about default data use and retention policies, explicit opt-in rather than opt-out for training data use, and clear user controls over autonomous actions like purchases to prevent confusion about what the system would do.

It is not established what specific harms resulted from these practices, whether users were unaware of these policies before signup, or what the legal or regulatory status of these practices is.

reports.title: Is Instinct safe to use? Three things to know before you sign up

summary:
# Summary

Instinct is a new AI personal assistant gaining popularity in Silicon Valley, but it presents significant privacy and security concerns that users should understand before signing up. By default, Instinct can use personal information shared with it to train AI models unless users actively opt out or use the Vault feature. Additionally, even when users disconnect linked accounts like email or social media, Instinct may retain copies of previously indexed data indefinitely, meaning information continues to exist in the system without active access. Finally, the assistant can make purchases on users' behalf with stored payment methods, and if disputes arise, Instinct is not responsible for resolving them.

Norton highlights these risks and positions its own Norton Family Assistant as an alternative that prioritizes data privacy. Unlike Instinct, Norton Family Assistant does not use shared information to train AI models, and user data is not retained by AI providers. The assistant requires explicit user confirmation before taking actions like submitting forms or making purchases, and users can easily delete their data. Norton emphasizes that AI assistants can be helpful without requiring users to sacrifice their personal data and security.
